body.x: A4LAB Inc. (CEO Jaeyeong Park) participated in the “Global Media Online Meetup” held on July 4 for Korean startups in collaboration with U.S. tech media outlet Ubergizmo.

The meetup, co-hosted by AVING News and Ubergizmo, focused on introducing the products and technologies of Korean companies and startups to the global market. It also highlighted CES 2026 Innovation Award applicants and participants to secure early media exposure and expand business opportunities.

A4LAB is a healthcare startup developing innovative surgical support solutions based on medical imaging and precision sensor technology. The company focuses on developing smart medical devices that ensure both patient safety and medical staff convenience, securing global competitiveness with its navigation system specifically designed for oral and maxillofacial surgery.

Its vision centers on simplifying complex medical procedures and enabling the same level of precision surgery in regions with limited healthcare access. To achieve this, A4LAB expands clinical partnerships and global collaboration networks, turning advanced technology into practical, field-ready solutions. It positions itself as a company dedicated to patient-centered, innovation-driven, and global-oriented healthcare standards.

The company has built a foundation for domestic and overseas expansion, actively validating its technology and engaging in global promotions. In Korea, A4LAB has partnered with leading universities and specialty hospitals, successfully conducting over 500 clinical cases to prove the accuracy and stability of “XAVE AIR.” This has earned the trust of medical professionals and paved the way for commercialization.

Internationally, the company has conducted promotional activities in Asia and North America. At FORIL 2025 in Jakarta, Indonesia, A4LAB showcased its product to local medical experts and buyers, verifying its market potential. In the U.S., it introduced XAVE AIR to investors and medical professionals through a global meetup program, laying the groundwork for partnership expansion.

Through both domestic and international clinical validation and promotional activities, A4LAB has established an early foothold for market entry and expects short-term results and full-scale overseas expansion.
XAVE AIR is a surgical navigation system that achieves sub-millimeter precision by integrating CT and MRI scans with 3D facial scans through proprietary software.

Instead of invasive bone fixation, it uses dental supports and skin markers to achieve high accuracy in a non-invasive way. Installation time is less than one minute, improving surgical efficiency. Clinical trials involving more than 500 cases have demonstrated its stable performance with no errors. A cloud-based remote support function enables collaboration among medical staff worldwide. The company states that this standard-setting solution is accessible even to small hospitals and developing regions.

The device adopts a compact, modular design for maximum space efficiency in small operating rooms. Dental supports provide ergonomic comfort for patients, while simple skin markers do not hinder surgical access. Its interface offers color-coded 3D visualization, allowing surgeons to identify anatomical structures intuitively.

The external design features smooth curves and neutral tones to minimize visual impact, while premium medical-grade materials enable sterilization and repeated use. This balances aesthetics with practicality.

XAVE AIR presents an alternative to conventional, costly, and invasive navigation systems, achieving sub-millimeter precision without bone fixation. Cloud connectivity allows real-time surgical support from remote experts, overcoming geographic barriers. In education, it can serve as a simulation tool for students and residents to train in navigation safely. Its low-cost, high-efficiency structure highlights its innovation in expanding access to advanced medical technology.

This global problem-solving capacity is particularly significant. Precision surgical navigation has been limited so far to large hospitals due to high equipment costs and a shortage of specialists. XAVE AIR’s lightweight, affordable, non-invasive design bridges this gap, enabling precision surgeries even in small hospitals and developing regions. The remote support function enables regions with limited medical resources to receive real-time guidance from world-class experts. Educational use also boosts the capabilities of future surgeons, contributing to the advancement of global medical standards.

Building on this technology, A4LAB plans a stepwise global market strategy. Domestically, it will continue joint research with hospitals to gather more clinical data and strengthen the commercialization foundation.

Internationally, the company is prioritizing FDA approval for U.S. market entry, while expanding collaborative research and education programs with Indonesian institutions to strengthen its position in Southeast Asia. Mid- to long-term plans include strategic hubs in Cairo (Egypt) and Dubai (UAE) to expand into Africa and the Middle East.

To enhance global promotion and partnerships, A4LAB will continue to join major international exhibitions. Starting with CES 2026 in Las Vegas, the company also plans to participate in Arab Health 2026 (Dubai), MEDICA 2026 (Germany), and Hospital Expo Jakarta 2026 (Indonesia), where it will present XAVE AIR to medical experts and buyers worldwide.

A4LAB has also applied for the CES 2026 Innovation Award. The company stated, “This challenge represents an important opportunity for us to gain global recognition for our unique technology and competitiveness. CES can serve as a bridgehead for entering the global medical device market, and winning the Innovation Award would demonstrate our credibility and technical strength to international buyers, investors, and medical experts. It would also increase brand awareness and expand international partnerships, potentially leading to export contracts and collaborative research. Through this challenge, we aim to achieve tangible results and expand our global network.”
Alongside global network expansion, A4LAB also expressed its ambition to enhance technology reliability and achieve real export contracts.

Founded in 2005, Ubergizmo runs Silicon Valley Post and publishes in six languages across 200 countries, focusing on electronics and technology. It covers major exhibitions such as CES, IFA, and MWC. Ubergizmo CTO Hubert Nguyen, a former NVIDIA programming engineer and 3D graphics developer, attended the event and has reported annually from CES on global companies’ products and technologies.
